candidates.how: The Experience Modernization Agent, Adobe's AI development agent for Edge Delivery Services and part of the Brand Experience Agent, reads a Figma component or frame through its Figma import add-on, which calls Figma's API through an MCP server. It turns the design's colors, typography, spacing and variables into the site's design tokens and its components into blocks or block variants, builds a new page from a Figma frame, and can redesign a site during migration with Figma as the design source and the live site as the content source. It also works for Experience Manager authoring projects, where it generates the block definitions. Each person stores their own Figma personal access token in the console, the agent works one component or frame at a time, and code reaches the site through the Git repository after a developer reviews it.
candidates.gain: The site built from the design files: approved Figma components become the site's blocks and design tokens, and Figma frames become pages authors can edit, so a redesign starts from the designers' files instead of screenshots.
candidates.notes: Connection id figma-eds (outside, line native); offer Figma on the AEM play (bv, so, eds) and Create your own play. Kind native: Figma import (add-on excat-figma@excat-extended) is an optional capability of Adobe's agent, turned on per project, and nothing is installed in Figma; under a strict reading of 'Adobe-provided plugin' it could be called extension. Suggested label: The Experience Modernization Agent's Figma import builds blocks, design tokens and pages. Availability: access to the Experience Modernization Console comes through the Adobe account team, which confirms entitlement, commercial terms and the AI credit allowance; credits count for each page uploaded to Experience Workspace or the author instance, not for prompts, and a restyle needs no upload. No beta or early access label on the Figma pages; release notes list Figma block migration for AEM authoring (2026.06.23), better Figma page migration (2026.08.06) and a Home page prompt for a page from Figma (2026.09.17). Prerequisites: console access through the Adobe account team; a Dev or Full Figma seat per person (View or Collab seats can read files through Figma's API only a few times a month); each person's own read-only Figma personal access token in the console's Settings under Credentials (there is no organization-wide Figma connection, and a token reads every file its owner can open); Figma import turned on for the project; write access to the site's Git repository, with branch protection so a developer approves each pull request; your client approves what the agent sends to the AI model for each frame or component (its structure, a screenshot, its variables and its text).
